title: TechDesk — SaaS Ticket Management Portal
excerpt: End-to-end SaaS helpdesk portal: tickets, users, real-time SignalR chat, embeddable chatbot, and Gemini-powered ticket summaries — led as Technical Lead on a three-person team.
overview: TechDesk is a SaaS ticket-management portal built for companies that need one place to track user and customer issues, assign ownership, and resolve them without bouncing between tools. Over roughly six months in 2024 I led the project end to end as Technical Lead on a three-person team — owning architecture, technical decisions, UI direction, and mentoring a junior engineer through delivery. The product covers ticket and user management, real-time conversation on issues, an embeddable chatbot for client sites, and AI assistance to summarize ticket threads. The goal was simple: let support teams close the loop on problems faster, including from the customer’s own website without forcing a clunky login experience.
challenges: Shipping an embeddable chatbot as a script that other sites could drop in — without weakening auth or leaking trust boundaries between TechDesk and the host application
Making ticket conversations feel real-time (not refresh-and-hope) across portal chat and the embedded widget, using SignalR reliably under multi-user load
Adding AI summary for ticket threads in a way that was useful for agents, without turning the product into an unfocused AI demo
Keeping a clean three-layer architecture and delivery discipline while the product grew from a small start into a full SaaS admin experience (tickets, users, branding, settings, dashboard)
approach: Owned end-to-end technical architecture and day-to-day engineering decisions: API shape, Angular module structure, auth model, Azure hosting, and how new features fit the existing three-layer design
Built real-time ticket chat with SignalR so agents and users could continue conversations live inside the portal
Delivered the embeddable chatbot as a standalone Angular component compiled to a single JS file clients can include on their own sites

Designed a TechDesk-owned SSO/OAuth path for the embed: validate credentials in TechDesk when the user already exists; for first-time users, call the integrating app’s verification API, then create the TechDesk user and continue the chat — so customers are not interrupted by a separate username/password wall when identity is already trusted
Secured regular portal APIs with JWT, and treated the embed surface as its own trust boundary with dedicated endpoints the widget is allowed to call
Integrated Gemini to summarize ticket/chat context for agents, and used Chart.js on the dashboard for operational visibility
Deployed and maintained the app on Azure App Service with Azure DevOps pipelines for consistent builds and releases; guided the junior engineer through reviews and implementation patterns
outcomes: Clients can embed the chatbot on their own sites and start support conversations with auth that respects the integrating app — without breaking the user’s flow
Agents get a unified portal for tickets, users, live chat, and AI summaries instead of stitching tools together manually
A maintainable SaaS foundation (branding, settings, role-based admin views, Azure hosting) that a small team could extend without rewriting the core
Clear technical ownership and mentoring practices that kept architecture decisions consistent as features landed
